attributes.fullTitle: Constructores de Paz: Una estrategia de reincorporación social y económica para la reconciliación y fortalecimiento del desarrollo local
attributes.description: The general objective is to contribute to the social and economic reintegration of ex-combatants, fostering reconciliation with the community in the municipalities of Fonseca and Manaure. The focus is on developing productive projects in the construction sector with a comprehensive, inclusive, and territorial approach. This action is part of the main proposal for social and economic reintegration in the Colombian Caribbean, linked to housing construction and rehabilitation and productive environments. Activities aim to complement and strengthen this reintegration strategy, generating skills and impacting regional reconciliation and local development. The initiative improves conditions for the reintegrated population, boosts the construction sector, and promotes employability in the border region, initially benefiting both ETCR populations, their families, and surrounding communities through job training. In a second phase, the establishment of productive units in the construction sector will provide employment and income opportunities for ex-combatants and local communities.

attributes.fullTitle: Promoting evidence-based media coverage of labour migration from Ukraine to V4 countries
attributes.description: The project is aimed at widespreading in popular media of detailed and argumentative data about the new labour legislation in V4 countries, methods of legal employment, sources of statistical data and expert interpretation. International team of researchers from Ukraine, Poland, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary will create a guide “Myths and stereotypes about Ukrainian labour migration to V4 countries”, covering media image of labour migration from Ukraine in media of 5 countries, analyzing the most common mistakes and myths, providing sources of trusted data for journalists, state officials and public persons who intend to make public statements about labour migration. Project includes a workshop-presentation for Ukrainian journalists and experts in Kyiv with participation of foreign co-authors of the guide, and a series of presentations of the guide in V4 countries’ capitals. Also Europe without Barriers will coordinate a 3-month competition for Ukrainian journalists in 5 categories: the best analytic publication, best explainer (“how to”), best reportage, best interview, best TV/radio program about labour migration to V4 countries.

attributes.label: Bordermng
attributes.dateBasis: Official project page places the project in 2019; exact duration not found.
attributes.fullTitle: Strengthening dialogue on border management between civil society and authorities
attributes.description: The field of border management has traditionally been perceived as a restrited security policy area with no room for democratic public participation. In 2019, the Government of Ukraine approved the Strategy for Integrated Border Management until 2025 which anticipates horizontal cooperation between all stakeholders within the border management processes. However, the involvement of civil society into the border management remains a new and unresolved issue. Local communities do not know how they can get involved in addressing border issues. The project aims to establish a dialogue between border management entities and representatives of border communities (Volyn, Lviv, Zakarpattia, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi, Odessa regions) and to initiate the exchange of professional information on border issues. The project envisages a series of online meetings and discussions with representatives of central government and local communities, the results and conclusions of which will be published in the public domain, as well as a number of media materials on the topic of the border management.

attributes.description: En la semana del 11 al 16 de agosto se desarrolló en la ciudad de Quito, Ecuador, el Encuentro Formativo de Mujeres convocado por Ecuador decide Mejor sin TLC, red que integra la Plataforma América Latina y el Caribe Mejor Sin TLC. La delegación internacional estuvo conformada por representantes de las Plataformas Argentina Mejor Sin TLC, Chile Mejor Sin TLC y Paraguay Mejor Sin Libre Comercio. Durante las jornadas de formación se compartieron espacios de intercambio y análisis con referentes de diversas organizaciones sociales y políticas del Ecuador y en las que se exigió la aparición de Julia Chuñil, activista mapuche por la defensa de 900 hectáreas de bosques nativos en peligro ante la avanzada de la industria forestal sobre tierras ancestrales mapuches con la complicidad del gobierno chileno. Julia Chuñil desapareció en noviembre de 2024 durante el gobierno de Gabriel Boric, quien ha hecho caso omiso a las exigencias de la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos (CIDH) y a las organizaciones sociales que exigen al Estado chileno intensificar su búsqueda. La desaparición de Julia Chuñil no es un caso aislado, ocurre en un contexto general de avanzada del neofascismo y de una izquierda inmovilizada carente de proyecto político y económico que aglutine a las mayorías trabajadoras.

attributes.label: Agro é Fogo Dossier
attributes.dateBasis: Dossier developed in phases; latest edition/release dated 13 Oct 2022.
attributes.description: Since August 19, 2019, the use of fire as a weapon has come to the forefront in conflicts in the Brazilian countryside. On that occasion, farmers conspired to set fire to and attack entire communities in southwestern Pará and their forest areas, in what became known as the “Day of Fire.” The case of the Terra Nossa Sustainable Development Project (PDS), in the same region, shows that this practice is systematic. This offensive by capital stands out and repeats itself: a year later, in 2020, the fire that ravaged the Pantanal also started in a coordinated manner on cattle ranches; three years later, in August 2022, preparations for a new Day of Fire were discovered in Mato Grosso. To address this reality, which already existed before but is repeating itself and intensifying under the Bolsonaro government, the reflections of the Agro É Fogo Network prompted the Dom Tomás Balduíno Documentation Center of the Pastoral Land Commission (CEDOC/CPT), which, starting in 2021, began to register fires as one of the 18 forms of violence against land occupation and possession.

attributes.dateBasis: Attac Austria appears in a 2020 EU-Mercosur opposition statement and maintains a current campaign page.
attributes.description: The widespread resistance to agreements such as TTIP and CETA has not changed the substantive orientation of EU trade and investment policy. Currently, the EU Commission is negotiating agreements with around 90 countries on behalf of their governments. All of these agreements hinder decent working conditions for everyone. They impede sustainable agriculture and a healthy climate. They do not guarantee that people in their countries can publicly organize basic services and further expand the power of corporations and their influence on national laws. We want and need a future-proof trade and investment policy now more than ever – for all people, not just for a select few. Interventions in regulations serving the public interest, public services, and special rights to sue for corporations have no place in fair trade agreements!

attributes.label: Austria

Municipalities against TTIP, CETA and TiSA

attributes.label: Kettensäge stoppen!
attributes.dateBasis: Current campaign/event activity documented in 2026; exact launch day not established.
attributes.description: Under the guise of "reducing bureaucracy" and "enhancing competitiveness," the EU is currently implementing an unprecedented deregulation agenda that weakens key protections for people and the environment. They say "reducing bureaucracy"—and they mean our rights. With the proverbial chainsaw, crucial safeguards for people and nature are being destroyed in one fell swoop. Driven by corporate lobbyists, the EU Commission, and conservative and right-wing forces—not always in the same constellation, but always with the same brutal force.

attributes.label: Wettrüsten stoppen!
attributes.dateBasis: Launch event/date located
attributes.description: The signs point to an arms race. With multi-billion-euro defense packages and subsidies for arms manufacturers, the EU aims to become "war-ready" by 2030. Austria is following suit with a recovery plan for 2032+, which proposes increasing military spending to 2 percent of its economic output, amounting to over 12 billion euros per year. That's more than the annual budget for education or healthcare. But those who think solely in military terms neglect what creates long-term security: social infrastructure, climate justice, diplomacy, and global solidarity. We are convinced: weapons create crises, not peace.

attributes.label: Ab jetzt gibt’s Klimageld!
attributes.dateBasis: Dated campaign action/publication
attributes.description: For months, broad sections of civil society have been demanding the disbursement of the climate allowance that the German government promised in its 2021 coalition agreement. Now, at the initiative of the association "Sanktionsfrei" (Sanction-Free), a broad eco-social alliance – including Attac – is distributing a one-time payment of €139 to 1,000 people receiving citizen's income, basic income support, or housing allowance as an example. According to calculations, the sum of at least €139 paid out by the alliance would be due to every person in Germany as compensation for the CO2 pricing of recent years. For a family of four, this would amount to €556 – a noticeable financial relief. As the CO2 price rises, this amount increases accordingly each year and could create a necessary social balance.

attributes.label: RohstoffEnergieHunger stoppen!
attributes.dateBasis: Campaign adopted/announced in 2024 and remains current.
attributes.description: The climate catastrophe is approaching ever more rapidly. Respecting planetary boundaries requires a radical departure from growth-oriented economics. We need a circular economy that uses available resources sparingly. This necessitates a global reduction in raw material consumption . Not only oil and gas, but also many other raw materials must remain largely in the ground. An international raw materials agreement should establish upper limits for raw material consumption and ensure a fair distribution of resources.

attributes.label: Tax the Rich
attributes.dateBasis: Formal signature campaign start
attributes.description: In Germany, the wealthiest one percent of the population owns a third of the wealth. The poorer half together owns less than two percent. For decades, capital income has been taxed less and less, while earned income and consumption have been taxed more and more. As a result, the super-rich pay proportionally far less tax than average earners. Excessive wealth is destroying the social foundations of a democracy and making society increasingly unjust. With this petition, we call on the Bundestag to reinstate the wealth tax on all types of assets. This would halt the further increase of excessive wealth and reduce the accumulation of enormous fortunes.

attributes.label: Indigenous Leadership Exchange Program

attributes.description: The main aim of this program is to support initiatives of indigenous rights activists and community leaders from Russia in their efforts to establish contacts with indigenous communities, human rights, and environmental organizations, international human rights bodies, and development organizations abroad. The Batani foundation helps find resources and provides logistics for such exchanges, including traveling and online participation in international events.

attributes.label: Blue Community Berlin
attributes.dateBasis: Berlin became a Blue Community on 22 Mar 2018.
attributes.description: "Blue Community" is an international grassroots movement founded by Maude Barlow, the world-renowned Canadian water activist and recipient of the Right Livelihood Award (often called the Alternative Nobel Prize). The Blue Community movement is a response to the increasing water scarcity on our planet, as well as the unequal distribution of this vital resource. A Blue Community aims to realize the human right to water and basic sanitation at both local and global levels. While this human right was recognized by the United Nations (UN) in 2010, its actual implementation remains lacking in many places.

attributes.label: Initiative BlackRock-Tribunal
attributes.dateBasis: Initiative originated in 2019; first tribunal held in 2020.
attributes.description: The US company BlackRock, nicknamed "Black Rock," is the world's largest asset manager. Along with Vanguard and State Street, it belongs to the "Big Three" of US financial investors. They are inextricably linked. BlackRock's assets under management have now grown to more than $10 trillion. That's roughly three times the annual output of the German economy. This money is invested globally not only in the largest corporations across most sectors, but also with the biggest international auditors and rating agencies, as well as leading media outlets. Despite this, these financial giants remain virtually unknown to the public, as they avoid the limelight. For this reason, the 'BlackRock Tribunal Initiative' once again organized a conference on BlackRock and similar companies, following up on the 2020 "tribunal." The initiative itself states: We are accusing BlackRock on behalf of other shadow banks: 1. Destruction of economic and political democracy, violation of international law and human rights. 2. Price gouging in rents and ancillary costs, low wages for employees 3. Increased global risk of war due to profiteering in the most important arms companies of the USA and the EU 4. Profiteering in the major coal, lignite, and oil companies. Purchase of state-guaranteed bonds from insolvent fracking companies.

Young people are supported and encouraged in their commitment through, among other things, farm visits/weekends in nature, on social media, in podcasts, with actions at festivals, as well as through exchanges with decision-makers and BIPoC activists.

attributes.label: Journée d’action européenne contre l’impunité des multinationales

attributes.fullTitle: Journée d’action européenne contre l’impunité des multinationales
attributes.description: Human rights and environmental violations, unacceptable in EU countries, should be equally unacceptable in developing countries. This is the message sought by the ECCJ – European Coalition for Corporate Justice – present in 15 European countries and represented in France by the Citizens' Forum for CSR, whose members include CCFD-Terre Solidaire, SHERPA, Friends of the Earth, CRID, and Peuples Solidaires. In France, to illustrate the need to end corporate impunity, three photomontages are being circulated online and on social media. This triptych illustrates some common violations in developing countries within a French context. Demonstrations are also being organized in several European countries. Citizens are encouraged to sign the petition for the campaign "Rights for All, Rules for Multinationals" www.des-reglespour-les-multinationales.org EUROPEAN DAY OF ACTION AGAINST MULTINATIONAL IMPUNITY "From mercury pollution in South Africa to child labor in India, multinationals – including those based in Europe – continue to benefit from the lack of a legal framework regulating their operations," states Sandra Cossart, CSR Manager for the Sherpa association and coordinator of the "Rights for All, Rules for Multinationals" campaign. "However, there are currently no mandatory international mechanisms to ensure that these multinationals are held accountable for the violations they commit, or of which they are complicit." This is why ECCJ is asking the EU to take action to ensure that: European multinationals should be legally responsible for damage caused to people and the environment, both inside and outside the EU; European multinationals should demonstrate transparency and publish accurate information regarding their impacts on people and the environment; non-European citizens, whose rights have been violated by European companies, should have access to justice within the EU.

attributes.fullTitle: Unify: Bringing the EU together on climate action
attributes.description: “Unify: Bringing the EU together on climate action” aims to facilitate the effective and early transition of Member States across Europe to low carbon and resilient economies by unifying three key policy opportunities: programming of EU funds, National Energy and Climate Plans (NECPs) and national and the EU’s Long Term Strategies. Through its targeted activities in 10 Member States and at the EU level, the Unify project showcases that if these three key EU policy processes are consistent, ambitious and in line with the Paris Agreement objectives, they could help all EU Member States to step up climate action. Through underlining the importance of alignment between the national and the EU’s long term strategies, National energy and climate plans and the local level climate and energy action plans (SECAPs), the UNIFY project reminds the importance of consistency in climate action at different levels.

attributes.fullTitle: Comissão Episcopal para Ecologia Integral e Mineração (CEEM)
attributes.description: The Special Episcopal Commission for Integral Ecology and Mining (CEEM) is a body of the National Conference of Bishops of Brazil (CNBB), created in 2017, with the mission of advising bishops and the CNBB on the socio-environmental challenges caused by the predatory extractive model, proposing pastoral responses inspired by the paradigm of Integral Ecology. Illuminated by the encyclical Laudato Si' and the local context presented in its manifesto " Integral Ecology: a narrative to confront the planetary socio-environmental crisis ," we seek to promote a national project based on the defense of life and the care of Creation, the sharing of common goods, and intergenerational justice. Our mission is accomplished through supporting communities. We offer support to dioceses and communities affected by predatory extraction, encouraging the protection of their territories and rights; Knowledge Production. We develop and disseminate studies, public statements, and opinions that critically analyze the impacts of mining and large projects, highlighting the responsibility of companies and public authorities; Political Advocacy. We work with the executive, legislative, and judicial branches in Brazil and participate in international forums, such as the UN Human Rights Commission and dialogues in the Vatican, to defend biomes, indigenous peoples, and our Common Home; Networking. We work in partnership with organizations such as the Churches and Mining Network, the Conference of Religious of Brazil and Latin America (CRB and CLAR), and social movements to strengthen solidarity and the search for alternatives to the extractive model.

attributes.label: Real Zero Europe Campaign
attributes.dateBasis: Real Zero Europe campaign statement/launch in 2022; campaign remains active.
attributes.description: To avoid the worst effects of climate chaos, we must radically transform, equitably and justly, the way we produce our food, manage our ecosystems, and power our economies. We must urgently deploy real and proven, socially just and people-led solutions and dramatically reduce greenhouse gas emissions at source, down to Real Zero. Real Zero Europe is a campaign bringing together climate, environmental, economic justice, human rights, and food sovereignty organisations, to scrap the European Commission’s carbon removal certification law, to resist Europe’s ‘net zero’ false solutions, and to apply pressure on the EU and European nations to take action now towards real, deep emissions cuts.

attributes.label: Fossil Free Europe Campaign
attributes.dateBasis: Friends of the Earth Europe described Fossil Free Europe as a new campaign around 2017; subsequent activity continues.
attributes.description: he fossil fuel era must end. We need an urgent and just transformation to a fossil-free Europe by 2030. Extraction and burning of coal, gas and oil is heating the planet and destroying communities, hitting the poorest hardest. People in the Global South, Black, Indigenous, People of Colour, women, youth, and those on low incomes are disproportionately affected. More than two-thirds of man-made greenhouse gas emissions come from the fossil fuel industry. They rake in billions in profits, while making the planet increasingly uninhabitable. European governments, pushed by the fossil fuel industry, continue to finance climate destruction, notably spending billions on fossil gas infrastructure. Friends of the Earth Europe campaigns to stop governments, the EU, and banks financing more fossil fuels – particularly through investments in fossil gas pipelines. We also hold fossil fuel companies to account, and work to cut them out of our political systems as part of our campaign for Fossil Free Politics.

attributes.label: VOICES

attributes.description: The GfbV stands up for the rights of ethnic, religious and linguistic autochthonous minorities and nationalities as well as for their minorities and nationalities as well as for the individual and collective rights of indigenous peoples. It is committed to the protection of civilian populations from the most serious human rights violations and to prevent crimes against humanity and genocide. We see human rights as universal, indivisible and inalienable. In accordance with our motto “A voice for those who have no voice”, the GfbV’s particular focus is on nationalities, minorities and indigenous peoples, as well as victims of severe human rights barely noticed by the public.

attributes.label: Beyond Bioenergy
attributes.dateBasis: Dated Beyond Bioenergy joint statement/action.
attributes.description: Forest loss threatens ecosystems and the lives, livelihoods, and traditions of many communities, disproportionately impacting women in all their diversity, Indigenous Peoples, and Afro-descendant and rural communities. It deepens gender inequalities, increases women’s burden of labour, and limits their access to resources and decision-making power. Our Gender Justice and Forests Campaign promotes decolonial, feminist approaches to forest conservation that centre the rights, knowledge, and leadership of women in all their diversity. We work with our members to dismantle intersecting systems of oppression, reduce gender gaps, and ensure inclusive, community-led forest governance that values care, equity, and collective power as essential to climate and environmental justice.

attributes.description: El acuerdo comercial Unión Europea-Mercosur intensificará la crisis climática provocada por la agricultura. La imagen de las llamas arrasando el Amazonas en agosto de 2019 hizo que las personas en todo el mundo se dieran cuenta de la conexión entre los agronegocios y la crisis climática. La selva estaba siendo quemada para dar lugar a la producción de carne, soja y otras materias primas agrícolas y así aumentar las ganancias de las corporaciones transnacionales de alimentos. Un importante motor de esta devastación es el comercio. Actualmente, un nuevo acuerdo comercial amenaza con aumentar aún más la expansión de los agronegocios en Brasil, con serias consecuencias para el clima.

attributes.description: Jubilee South Brazil launches the booklet “ Public Debt and Climate Crisis: Understanding the Impacts on Our Lives ,” a popular education material that aims to reflect on the relationship between the debt system and the effects of climate change—especially on historically oppressed peoples and communities. Among other things, it critically analyzes wind energy projects (onshore and offshore) and mining, showing that, even under the label of "clean energy," these ventures generate socio-environmental conflicts and directly affect the livelihoods of local populations. The booklet also highlights the role of women in the fight for climate justice and popular sovereignty, showing how gender, race, and class inequalities deepen in the face of the climate crisis and public debt. In this scenario, women are the most affected, whether by the overload of care work or by the intensified violence in the context of environmental disasters.

attributes.description: The municipal temporary shelter program “Barcelona Protects Journalists from Mexico” (PAT-P) aims to facilitate the temporary stay in Barcelona of members of this group who are threatened due to the exercise of their profession and their activism in denouncing human rights violations. Its purpose is to provide them with a period of respite and to strengthen their personal and professional capacities so they can better confront their situation, while also raising visibility and internationalizing their cause. Likewise, the program seeks to promote and consolidate a Catalonia–Mexico network of journalists that can help reinforce the work of journalists who are under threat.

attributes.description: The Free Trade Agreement between the European Union and Mercosur has been under negotiation for over 20 years between the two blocs, generating strong criticism and resistance from civil society organizations on both continents. These criticisms are based on the asymmetrical and detrimental nature of the Agreement for our country and our region. This Agreement would reinforce our dependence on the export of primary goods, while simultaneously opening the doors to European exports of high value-added industrial goods and heavily subsidized agro-industrial products. This would have serious consequences for our countries, their people, territories, and ecosystems, exacerbating global socio-environmental crises.

attributes.label: #Bestof49
attributes.dateBasis: Pulse of Europe identifies its #Bestof49 positions as of 7 Jan 2025 and lists #Bestof49 as an ongoing project; the project remained active in 2026.
attributes.description: The Conference on the Future of Europe (CoFoE), which took place from 2021 to 2022, was the EU’s largest project involving citizens. It resulted in 49 proposals aimed at making the EU more democratic, sustainable, and citizen-focused. Pulse of Europe (PoE) has selected some of these ideas for its ‘#Bestof49’ campaign, in which it actively advocates for their implementation in concrete European policy. This includes, for example, the demand to abolish the principle of unanimity in EU Council decisions. As part of this effort, Pulse of Europe issued a single open letter to Bundestag members and candidates across most constituencies, bringing the European discussion to the local level and underlining the need for a strong, united and sustainable European Union.

attributes.label: European HomeParliaments
attributes.dateBasis: A contemporary September 2018 report documents the first European HomeParliaments round already underway; Pulse of Europe's current EHP site documents subsequent rounds through 2025 and continued participation.
attributes.description: Pulse of Europe (PoE) developed the ‘European HomeParliaments’ as a new participation format to directly involve citizens in European debates. By September 2025, already ten rounds had taken place. In small groups, participants meet in person or online, perhaps in someone's living room, to discuss three selected EU policy proposals, vote on them and submit their results to a shared platform, which forms a collective pulse of public opinion. Supported by individual European politicians who engage with the outcomes, this format offers citizens a low-threshold, structured dialogue that connects grassroots discussion with real political processes.

attributes.label: Pride of Europe
attributes.dateBasis: Pulse of Europe's project page explicitly states that the campaign has been running since 2019 and labels it as an ongoing project.
attributes.description: The ‘Pride of Europe’ campaign, organised by Pulse of Europe (PoE), responds to rising nationalism and the erosion of LGBTI rights in several EU member states. It does this by drawing public attention to the issue and supporting local human rights movements, especially in Eastern and Southeastern Europe. As part of the campaign, the initiative created the European Rainbow Flag, which was funded through a large-scale crowdfunding campaign, and raised in dozens of European cities. The campaign also launched the ‘To Poland with Love’ petition in response to the so-called LGBT-free zones.
